method: Looks for the SHAPE of an untested assumption rather than re-running known tests. Proposes attacks; never executes them.

hypotheses.target: Deploy smoke test (blank-page class, rendered DOM)
hypotheses.attack: Break it deliberately and confirm the build fails. The registry names a test but audit.mjs never runs it, so nothing checks that this guard still works.
hypotheses.why: Our own law: a guard is not real until breaking it fails the build. An unexercised guard is a comfort, not a control.

hypotheses.attack: Corrupt it — empty object, missing top-level key, wrong types — and see which of its 3 readers notices. Then decide which of them SHOULD have.
hypotheses.why: Read by 3 scripts and validated by none. A silent shape change here propagates everywhere before anything complains.

hypotheses.target: the sealed index (our own measurement only — nothing external corroborates the level)
hypotheses.attack: Find one independent way to sanity-check this number, even a crude one. If none exists, say so on the methodology page rather than letting a reader assume corroboration we do not have.
hypotheses.why: A figure only one source can confirm is a single point of failure wearing a VERIFIED chip.

hypotheses.attack: Run the pipeline with the clock set to 23:59 UTC on the last day of a month, and again at 00:01 on the first. Confirm nothing double-counts, skips a day, or writes two entries for one date.
hypotheses.why: 20 scripts slice UTC dates into day keys. Month and year boundaries are where that quietly goes wrong, and no test covers it.
